name: Eat App Review Management
oneLiner: Review management add-on inside Eat App, a Dubai-based restaurant reservation, table management and guest CRM platform; it gathers reviews into one view, lets staff reply in the app and asks guests for reviews after their visit.
bestFor: Restaurants already using (or choosing) Eat App for reservations and guest CRM that want basic review monitoring and replies in the same system, rather than a standalone reputation platform.

updates.text: Acquired ReserveGo, an Indian table reservation platform serving more than 1,000 restaurants (acquisition dated June 2025 by PitchBook; announced publicly in January 2026).
Raised a $10M Series B extension led by PSG Equity through its portfolio company Zenchef, and announced a Swiggy partnership in India selling Eat App's growth suite as GroMax.

features: Reviews from Google, Facebook and more in one searchable dashboard, filtered by keyword, platform or star rating
Reply to reviews from inside Eat App, with response tracking and reminders; reply to reviews and messages by SMS, WhatsApp or email
AI sentiment analysis and review summaries
Reports on average rating, review volume and response rates, plus a time-stamped review activity feed
Smart rules that automate responses, flag important feedback and alert the team
Post-dining surveys (Core and up) and Review at table QR codes on tables or receipts (Pro and up)
Built on Eat App's reservations, table management and guest CRM, so reviews sit next to guest profiles and visit history
Online bookings from partner channels (e.g. Mozrest, Tripadvisor) flow into the same system

pricing.text: Review management (read and reply to Google reviews) is included in the Core, Pro and Enterprise plans. Billed monthly / yearly per venue: Lite $99 / $69 per month (no review management), Core $199 / $159, Pro $389 / $299 (adds Review at table, loyalty, POS integration), Enterprise for groups of 8 or more venues by quote. Free plan limited to 100 guests a month. 14-day free trial of any plan. POS and payment integrations $39 per month extra on Core. Prices as shown in USD; they may vary by region.

notes: November 2026: restaurant.eatapp.co/pricing and /review-management read with curl. The plan table shows review management ('Read and reply to your Google reviews') on Core, Pro and Enterprise, not on Lite or Free; Review at table and the loyalty suite on Pro and Enterprise. Prices shown in USD from this location; Eat App says they vary by region. Bing is no longer named on the review management page, so it was dropped. G2 rating from a search-result snippet (4.7 from 40 reviews) and covers Eat App as a whole. PSG/Zenchef led the January 2026 round; this is an investment, not an acquisition, as far as sources show (CB Insights dates the investment July 2025). Caution: older Eat App material describes sending only high-rating guests to Google (review gating), which Google's policies discourage; the current pages weren't checked for this, so the review doesn't describe the routing. Customer names come from 2021 Eat App press materials.
pros: Reviews sit in the same guest CRM as reservations and visit history
Published prices, a free plan and a 14-day free trial of any paid plan
AI sentiment analysis, review summaries and rules that flag important feedback
Eat App as a whole holds 4.7 out of 5 on G2

cons.text: Review management isn't sold alone; it comes with Eat App's Core plan ($199 per month, or $159 billed yearly) and up
The plan comparison describes replies for Google reviews; other sites are named only as 'Facebook and more'
Review at table QR codes and the loyalty suite need the Pro plan ($389 per month, or $299 billed yearly)
Built for restaurants that run reservations on Eat App, so a group on another booking system would run two platforms

plans.billing: per month, billed monthly or yearly (yearly saves up to 30%)
